sense: of one’s own country, not foreign

terms.gloss: of one’s own country, native, internal (opposed to foreign)
evidence: Cic. Off. 2.26: externa libentius in tālī rē quam domestica recordor
Caes. BG 2.10.4: domesticae cōpiae reī frūmentāriae (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Against externus or peregrīnus (see foreign): one’s own people’s customs, examples, resources, enemies; bellum domesticum, civil war (Lewis & Short). Its first sense is “of the household” (see domestic, of the home and family).

terms.gloss: internal, within the state (of war, strife, evils)
evidence: Cic. Cat. 2.28: bellum intestīnum ac domesticum
terms.comment: “Inward, internal”, of trouble inside the state: bellum intestīnum, discordia intestīna (Lewis & Short). As a noun, intestīna are the guts.

phrases.latin: Externa libentius in tālī rē quam domestica recordor.
phrases.english: In a matter like this I prefer to recall foreign examples rather than our own.

phrases.latin: bellum intestīnum ac domesticum post hominum memoriam crūdēlissimum et maximum
phrases.english: the cruellest and greatest civil war within the memory of man

sources: Lewis & Short: domesticus · Lewis & Short: intestinus
